Siemens SIMATIC S7 PLCs Web Server

🌐 Source: Cisa • 📅 22 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 3020 min read (604081 words, 📚 Deep Dive)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • View CSAF Summary SIMATIC S7-1500 devices contain multiple vulnerabilities in the web server that could allow an attacker to execute malicious code in an authorized user’s browser session and perform PLC operations within the scope of that user’s authorization.
  • Industry observers note that SIMATIC S7-1500 devices contain multiple vulnerabilities in the web server that could allow an attacker to execute malicious code in an authorized user’s browser session and perform PLC operations within the scope of that user’s authorization.
  • The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 PLCs Web Server are affected:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

View CSAF Summary SIMATIC S7-1500 devices contain multiple vulnerabilities in the web server that could allow an attacker to execute malicious code in an authorized user’s browser session and perform PLC operations within the scope of that user’s authorization. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available. The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 PLCs Web Server are affected: SIMATIC Drive Controller CPU 1504D TF (6ES7615-4DF10-0AB0) vers:all/* (CVE-2026-63350, CVE-2026-63351, CVE-2026-63352, SIMATIC Drive Controller CPU 1504D TF (6ES7615-4DF10-0AB0) 2 Vulnerabilities Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection'), Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') Background Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide Company Headquarters Location: Germany Vulnerabilities Expand All + CVE-2026-63350 Affected devices do not properly restrict executable content contained in imported trace files. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted trace file. Successful exploitation could allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the user’s browser session and perform PLC operations through the web server within the scope of the user’s authorization. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files None availableCurrently no fix is available Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-95 Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 9.6 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H View CVE Details CVE-2026-63351 Affected devices do not properly validate and sanitize visual properties of calculated signals contained in imported CSV trace files before rendering them on the Trace page. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted trace file. Successful exploitation could allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the user’s browser session and perform PLC operations through the web server within the scope of the user’s authorization. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files None availableCurrently no fix is available Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-63352 Affected devices do not properly sanitize calculated signal data contained in imported CSV trace files before rendering it on the Trace page. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted trace file. Successful exploitation could allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the user’s browser session and perform PLC operations through the web server within the scope of the user’s authorization. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted trace file. Successful exploitation could allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the user’s browser session and perform PLC operations through the web server within the scope of the user’s authorization. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files None availableCurrently no fix is available Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-63356 Affected devices do not properly sanitize calculated signal names contained in imported CSV trace files before including them in error messages on the Trace page. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted trace file. Attacker-controlled JavaScript could be executed in the user’s browser session when the resulting error message is displayed. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files None availableCurrently no fix is available Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N View CVE Details CVE-2026-63357 Affected devices do not properly sanitize calculated signal data contained in imported calculated signal files before rendering it on the Trace page. This could allow an attacker to social engineer an authorized user who holds the function right “Read diagnostics” into importing a specially crafted file. Successful exploitation could allow attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the user’s browser session and perform PLC operations through the web server within the scope of the user’s authorization. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files None availableCurrently no fix is available Additional Metrics Relevant CWE: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String 3.1 6.1 MEDIUM CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N View CVE Details Acknowledgments Siemens ProductCERT reported these vulnerabilities to CISA. General Recommendations As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity Additional Resources For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories Terms of Use The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use. Recommended Practices CISA recommends customers take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities. Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet. Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks. When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices. CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures. CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies. CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets. Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies. Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory. Industry observers note that SIMATIC S7-1500 devices contain multiple vulnerabilities in the web server that could allow an attacker to execute malicious code in an authorized user’s browser session and perform PLC operations within the scope of that user’s authorization. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7 PLCs Web Server are affected:.

Product Status: known_affected.

MitigationDisable the webserver if not required on the affected systems. Restrict the access to Port 80/tcp and 443/tcp to trusted IP address only.

MitigationEnsure only qualified personnel is authorized to access the web server.

MitigationOnly upload trusted trace files.

View CVE Details.

In a recent development, as a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity.

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories.

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.
